title: Fit the hint to the kind of miss
statement: Fit a recall hint to the kind of miss, naming a near spelling or another taught word rather than just saying wrong, and give the word on the second miss.
example: A typed word within an edit distance of two is told it is nearly right instead of being given a letter.
detail: The lesson engine's key-word deck copies a 3D version's gap rules in code: a typed word within an edit distance of two of the answer is told it is nearly right, a word from the same deck is shown its own meaning beside the cued one, anything else gets the answer's first letter, and the second miss gives the word with its meaning (`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/key-words.js`). A test plants a near spelling and a mix-up within the deck and checks each line (`g9/transformer/test/mechanics.test.mjs`).
against: The last hint gives away part of the answer: `The word you want begins with "${w.word.charAt(0).toUpperCase()}".` (`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/key-words.js`, line 121). Nothing measures whether these hints help recall. Whether the slip counts differs by task: in say it back "a near spelling of a long word is named but not counted as a miss" (g9/transformer/src/mechanics/say-it-back.js line 3), while in key words a near spelling "gets a nudge, since a taught word is spelled right" (g9/transformer/src/mechanics/key-words.js line 4) and comes back marked wrong (line 122).
